items.correction: WCAG 1.4.10 (Reflow) asks for 320 CSS px wide for content that scrolls down, like this site; its 256 px height is the case for content that scrolls sideways, such as vertical text. So 320 × 256 is not WCAG's own test for this page. It is, though, exactly what a 1280 × 1024 screen shows at 400% zoom, and at that size the card loses its question. The finding holds: the problem is lost content in a zoomed, 320 px-wide window, not a 256 px rule.

items.central_claim_check: The spec bounds the card's width (lines 170-171) and never its height; section 9 (Testing) has no short or zoomed window. WCAG 2.2's Understanding page for 1.4.10 (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html) gives the rule as 'Vertical scrolling content at a width equivalent to 320 CSS pixels; Horizontal scrolling content at a height equivalent to 256 CSS pixels', says '320 CSS pixels is equivalent to a starting viewport width of 1280 CSS pixels wide at 400% zoom', and lists failure F102, 'content disappearing and not being available when content has reflowed'. A fixed card does not move when the page scrolls, so anything above the window's top edge cannot be reached.
